text:
kai: Saw a perf regression on PP 8x2 after the kernel-selection change — p95 latency up ~25% on 8k seq runs. Periodic stalls, looks like all-reduce pileups. Anyone else hitting this?

mira: yeah, I hit it on canary last night. Quick perf trace shows a few large gaps between compute kernels where NCCL waits pile up.

devon: can you paste the trace or command you used? pinging @perf-bot in case there's an auto-attach.

perf-bot: attached summary from /artifacts/pp8x2/1775006700/trace.json — per-stage breakdown (avg): allreduce=12.3ms, compute=3.4ms, idle=8.9ms; spikes up to 52ms on some ranks.

mira: initial analysis: kernel-selection patch picked a GEMM tiling kernel with slightly higher launch latency for small M/N -> increases per-step compute time and ruins comm/compute overlap. Also continuous-batching heuristic flushes on token boundaries causing microbatch imbalance across stages.

kai: tried increasing microbatch from 4->8 and adjusted 1F1B buffering. Throughput +12% but tail p99 still bad. Here's a rough ASCII timeline from the trace:

  rank0: [C+++][AR----][idle---][C+++][AR----]  
  rank1: [idle--][C++][AR---][C++][AR---]

(where AR=allreduce, C=compute). You can see misalignment.

ana: could KV cache misses be adding unexpected work and shifting boundaries?

mira: KV miss rate is tiny (~1.2%), not the driver. The root is scheduling + microbatch frag.

devon: quick mitigation proposal: add a tiny rendezvous window (<=200us) before flushing a microbatch so NCCL collective calls can coalesce across ranks. Branch: pp-rendezvous-delay, PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/3112. Also a fallback to previous kernel if microbatch < 6.

kai: testing pp-rendezvous-delay on canary now. If it helps we can prod backport.

perf-bot: new canary run (pp-rendezvous-delay) summary: p95 reduced from 430ms -> 330ms, avg throughput +6%, allreduce wall time median -30%. p99 improved but still +8% vs baseline.

mira: promising. Followups: 1) run 1F1B schedule with two-step warmup (microbatch ramp) and kernel backoff policy; 2) add telemetry: per-stage idle time, microbatch size distribution, per-call kernel-id to detect bad combos automatically.

devon: noted. I'll add trace labels for kernel-id and microbatch-size in the profiler output.

kai: I'll open a short RFC with experiment matrix (microbatch sizes [4,6,8,12], rendezvous windows [0,100,200]us, kernel backoff on small batches) and assign tester slots. cc @mira @devon.

mira: also let's add an E2E test that runs long sequences (>=8k) on PP 8x2 overnight to catch regresses early.

kai: agreed — creating job now. Thanks all :thumbsup:
